gen-gf-comic-neue-gf-orbit: Friendly and loose, Comic Neue writes like a quick note. Orbit follows in a plain sans, each character floating apart, so the casual heading gets a tidy, spaced-out partner underneath.
gen-gf-comic-neue-gf-padyakke-expanded-o: Comic Neue's casual, rope-thin pen lettering is the first thing you notice. Padyakke Expanded One, a text serif with wide-mouthed c shapes, gives the weight and gravity that the handwriting happily leaves to it.
gen-gf-comic-neue-manrope: Pen-and-paper looseness is what defines Comic Neue, with its thin, rope-like outline and open curves. Manrope handles the structured side, and its bright gaps at each curve's mouth keep the text clean and approachable.
gen-gf-comic-neue-montserrat: Casual and hand-drawn, with a wiry outline that never thickens or thins. Comic Neue is best big and brief, while Montserrat in plain sans form handles the rest.
gen-gf-comic-neue-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall in a plain sans, its soaring x-height and wide e never squeezed shut. And Comic Neue's handwriting above it gives that crisp body a friendly, inviting counterpoint.
gen-gf-comic-neue-switzer: Switzer brings Swiss restraint in a plain sans, with tubular, wire-like letters and a tall waist line, under a handwritten heading. Loose pen lettering meets tidy structure.
gen-gf-comic-neue-work-sans: Comic Neue brings casual handwriting with open c forms, while Work Sans sets a contemporary sans-serif below it with a high mean line. Their handwritten-versus-modern gap is the pair's best feature.
gen-gf-comic-relief-crimson-pro: Comic Relief has no visible difference between its up and side strokes, giving it a bold, steady, technical-pen look. Crimson Pro then carries a long page gently, its subtle thick-and-thin cadence making a classic serif feel refined.
gen-gf-comic-relief-fs-neco: Commanding, blunt and ballpoint-drawn, Comic Relief takes the top spot. Neco, a classic serif, follows with a measured swell from hairline to stem, adding dignity beneath the heading's punch.
